newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Opposition makes poll gain on Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Opposition makes poll gain on Australia govt.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition has cut the government's opinion poll lead to five points -- the Liberal-National coalition's smallest lead since ousting Labor in 1996, according to a newspaper poll published on Tuesday.
The government's support dropped to 45 percent in the latest Newspoll, published in The Australian, from 49 percent in the last poll two weeks ago.
Labor's support increased two points to 40 percent.
The latest result compares with the coalition's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996, election.
Despite Labor's gain, opposition leader Kim Beazley continues to trail Prime Minister John Howard by 30 points as preferred prime minister, although the gap narrowed by two points.
Howard's backing as preferred prime minister fell one point to 53 percent and Beazley's increased one point to 23 percent. Another 24 percent of those surveyed were uncommitted.
The poll surveyed 1,149 voters around Australia by telephone over the last weekend.
